units.note: Greek has τοὺς ὄχλους (the levies/masses); English 'the young men' is an addition but not in the listed error classes; left alone.
ἐπὶ δόρυ = toward the spear side (right); 'by the right' is correct.

findings.quote: For although the citizens in democracies are generally more eager in military struggles than the civic subjects of tyrants, the mercenaries
findings.problem: Greek has the proportional correlative ὅσῳ … τοσούτῳ ('by as much as … by so much'): the more eager the democratic masses are than the tyrants' civic subjects, the more the monarchs' mercenaries surpass those of democracies. English turns it into a concessive 'although'.
findings.proposed_fix: For to the degree that the masses in democracies are more eager in military struggles than the citizens subject to tyrants, to that same degree the mercenaries

findings.quote: when the entire mercenary force had broken the Achaeans and the left wing had collapsed
findings.problem: τοῦ ξενικοῦ παντὸς ἐγκεκλικότος τοῖς Ἀχαιοῖς καὶ παραλελυμένου τοῦ λαιοῦ κέρως: the whole mercenary force of the Achaeans had given way and the left wing was broken up. English inverts the agent (mercenaries broke the Achaeans).
findings.proposed_fix: when the entire Achaean mercenary force had given way and the left wing had been broken up

findings.quote: he neither fled in panic nor withdrew in despair.
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna (***) after ἀπέστη, before ἀλλ᾽ ὑποστείλας; English reads on as if whole.
findings.proposed_fix: he neither fled in panic nor withdrew in despair [gap in the Greek text here].

findings.quote: he immediately ordered the front companies of the phalanx to wheel with locked shields and advance at the double
findings.problem: εὐθέως τοῖς πρώτοις τέλεσι … ἐπ᾽ ἀσπίδα κλίνων, προῆγε μετὰ δρόμου: Philopoemen himself wheeled the leading companies to the left (ἐπ᾽ ἀσπίδα = toward the shield side) and advanced at a run; 'locked shields' is not in the Greek.
findings.proposed_fix: he immediately wheeled the front companies of the phalanx to the left and advanced at the double

findings.quote: Polybius the Megalopolitan to gather the remaining Illyrians, armored troops, and mercenaries who had not joined in the flight
findings.problem: Πολυαίνῳ δ᾽ ἐπέταξε τῷ Μεγαλοπολίτῃ: the man is Polyaenus, not Polybius. Also τοὺς διακεκλικότας τὴν φυγήν = those who had turned/scattered in flight, the opposite of 'had not joined in the flight'.
findings.proposed_fix: Polyaenus the Megalopolitan to gather the survivors and the Illyrians, armored troops, and mercenaries who had scattered in flight

findings.quote: found himself beyond the enemy’s wing
findings.problem: ὑπερδέξιος τοῦ τῶν πολεμίων κέρατος means in a commanding position above/over the enemy's wing, not 'beyond' it.
findings.proposed_fix: found himself in a commanding position over the enemy’s wing

findings.quote: In just such situations it is the commanders who are most often exposed to the gravest danger.
findings.problem: Greek ends in a lacuna: ἐν οἷς δὴ καὶ μέγιστα συμβαίνει τοὺς ἡγουμένους *** ; the predicate is missing. English invents a complete sentence.
findings.proposed_fix: In just such situations it very often happens that the commanders [text breaks off here in the Greek].
